findings.description: The instance user data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data can be retrieved by principals with instance/metadata access and is commonly exposed through Terraform state, source repositories, or instance compromise, allowing misuse of the associated AWS identity.
Ingress permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploit attempts against the instance.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so its data may be stored unencrypted at rest unless account-level default encryption happens to be enabled outside this configuration.
The snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured for encryption. It therefore can preserve the volume's data without encryption at rest.
The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network metadata can therefore be stored without an explicit encryption-at-rest control.
